# Content-Security-Policy

The sources a site's Content-Security-Policy must allow for the widget, and what stops working without each.

From the help article "Allow the widget in your Content-Security-Policy" (`docs/help/widget/allow-the-widget-in-your-content-security-policy.md`, reviewed 2026-10-26). The same text answers in the Ask tab on opem.app.

## Which sources does the widget need in my Content-Security-Policy?

If your site sends a Content-Security-Policy, add these sources to it:

| Directive | Source | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `script-src` | `https://support.opem.app` | The widget's script |
| `connect-src` | `https://support.opem.app` | Opem's API: the project's settings, questions, requests and replies |
| `connect-src` | `https://vercel.com` | Uploading screenshots to Opem's private file storage |
| `connect-src` | `wss://ws-eu.pusher.com` | Live updates: your team's replies appearing while the Help panel is open |
| `img-src` | `blob:` | Showing screenshots, files and your project's logo in the widget |

For example:

```
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://support.opem.app; connect-src 'self' https://support.opem.app https://vercel.com wss://ws-eu.pusher.com; img-src 'self' blob:
```

The widget runs in your page, not in a frame, so `frame-src` needs nothing for it.

## What stops working if a source is missing?

- Without `script-src https://support.opem.app`, the widget does not load at all.
- Without `connect-src https://support.opem.app`, the Help button shows but cannot reach Opem: the widget falls back to its default look and nothing can be asked or sent.
- Without `connect-src https://vercel.com`, screenshots fail to upload; requests without screenshots still work.
- Without `connect-src wss://ws-eu.pusher.com`, everything works, but replies take up to 30 seconds to appear while the panel is open, instead of moments.
- Without `img-src blob:`, screenshots and files on requests do not show, and the Help panel shows the Opem mark instead of your logo.

Your browser's console names each source it refused.

## Why does the widget connect to Pusher?

Opem uses Pusher Channels to tell the widget when your team has replied, so the reply appears straight away. The widget connects only while the Help panel is open, and only for a person who has used requests in that browser before. The connection carries no cookies and nothing about the person: Opem's API signs one private channel for them, and every message on it is a request reference only. The reply itself is read from Opem's API.
